propositions: The divergent_implementation axis is mis-calibrated: it fires on only 7.72% of plan-v3 findings, is the only hard-override axis never receiving closed-literal grading, and misses ~90% of the omitted-scope-site class it exists to describe.

A G6 finding (c4ad-a93e-0613-408f) with four unenumerated s3vectors consumer sites scored impact=0.0 despite validity=0.8889 and block_threshold=0.60, because all seven impact axes were graded none; divergent_implementation was not applied to this omitted-scope case.

Replacing divergent_implementation's ordinal grades (none/low/medium/high) with a closed Literal (none/contradicts_reality/omits_required_site/incomplete_enumeration) and flooring only the two hard grades at 0.85 will block the target finding while routing incomplete-enumeration cases below every blocking threshold, matching the oracle-kind precedent.

The proposed prod_impact floor (Fix 2) collides structurally with the novelty_priority_floor convergence mechanism: it lifts an unbounded severity band whose consequences cannot be remediated by plan edits, causing non-terminating remediation loops; Fix 1 (semantic grading) is sufficient and reaches 26% of Fix 2's intended targets.

ADR 0054 mandates that calibration must be driven by the existing REVIEW_RESULT corpus sidecars and explicitly rejects purpose-built LLM eval suites and bulk re-review runs on cost grounds, narrowing ADR 0036's A/B clause to corpus replay and dogfood observation only.

Corpus-replay bracketing (pessimistic bound) shows the worst-case grade assignment produces 81 new blocks across 1,396 non-none-graded findings, far below the 113-finding over-fire from an ungraded blunt widening and within convergence tolerance; real outcome deferred to plan-v4 dogfooding per ADR 0054 §3(b).
